# jochwacht-sbom 0.14.0 — only what you actually ship

A Python lockfile holds the resolution for *every* environment the resolver
considered, not just the one that leaves your house. `uv.lock` writes one
package entry per resolution, each with its own markers. Until now all of
them were reported as components you ship — including the ones that can
never be installed on your target.

Tell the tool what you ship:

```bash
jochwacht-sbom . --target-env "python=3.10;platform=linux;arch=aarch64,x86_64"
```

Comma multiplies, semicolon separates the axes. Keys: `python`, `platform`,
`arch`, `system`, `os`, `implementation`. Read from `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`
and `requirements.txt`.

Measured on a real 128-package lockfile: six resolutions reach no target
environment — and their findings had been counted against code that is not
in the artefact, one of them rated CRITICAL.

## Nothing is deleted

A resolution no target reaches stays in the bill as `scope="excluded"`, with
the markers and the reason as properties. Your bill still agrees with your
lockfile, and an auditor can see that the resolution existed and why it does
not ship. Deleting it would have made the two disagree in silence.

## Nothing is guessed

A marker that needs something you did not declare — `platform_machine` when
you only gave `python` — is **not** evaluated. It counts as shipped, with a
note. The alternative would be to take the value from the machine running
the scan, and then the same lockfile would produce different bills on an x86
and an ARM build host.

Without `--target-env` nothing is evaluated and the output is unchanged.

## A limit worth knowing

`uv.lock` carries markers in two places: on the package entry and on
dependency edges. This release reads the first kind. On the lockfile above
that is 6 resolutions; a further 31 packages carry their only marker on an
edge and are still reported as shipped. Reading those needs reachability
through the dependency graph and comes separately.

## Also

- New dependency `packaging>=23.0` for the marker evaluation. If it is
  missing, markers are not evaluated and everything counts as shipped, with
  a warning — never a crash.
- The run now distinguishes the two reasons a component can be
  `scope="excluded"`: test/example material and dev tooling on one side, an
  unreachable target environment on the other. Calling the second one "test
  material" would be a false statement about your project.
